- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) and forecast is flat or declining, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 3–5 days to capture mean reversion lag.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misreads trend direction; use 3-period moving average of sentiment to guide forecast direction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, not 30-day trend.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome in 3–5 consecutive days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias for next 3–7 days to capture lagged momentum.
